reader.requirement: At 1985 (with the 1989 Intrinsic Function amendment) argument-1 of FUNCTION COS must be a numeric argument, i.e. an arithmetic expression (numeric literal, numeric elementary item, numeric or integer function, or an expression over them); any operand not of class numeric (alphanumeric, alphabetic, numeric-edited, group, nonnumeric literal, SPACE, ALL literal) must be refused.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 IntroducedIn/RemovedIn window: the function is available at 85 (IntroducedIn 85), so no refusal
ArgPredicate.AppliesAt(edition year) for per-position predicates; the Uniform rows of COS/FACTORIAL/INTEGER-PART carry none, so the class screen is the same code at every edition

reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f35_01 exercises only the legal half (literal, data item, expression); the refusal of non-numeric classes is probed here

probes.printed: COBOL1627 x7: PIC X, "1", numeric-edited, group, SPACE, PIC A, ALL "1" each refused (class alphanumeric/alphabetic; requires class numeric, §2023:15.20.3 r1)
probes.expected: each refused: none is class numeric (§1989:A.2.2 AR1)
accepted: arithmetic expressions over packed, binary, signed scaled, subscripted items, a numeric function, ZERO; values per the returned-value rules

reader.notes: The class screen (Verified row 'n') refuses every non-numeric operand class at 85 and admits every arithmetic-expression form. The messages cite §2023:15.20.3 r1 even at --std 85. The cosbad probe also drew a COBOL0900 for its own numeric-edited VALUE literal, which is correct at 85 and unrelated.

refuter.evidence: The reader's cosbad/fnok2 probes do not cover a 1985 operand class that is numeric-looking but not class numeric, or a later edition's literal. I probed: ixarg.cob: COS (IXD), where IXD is USAGE INDEX, was refused with COBOL6979, citing §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR5 (OK: 'can be referenced explicitly only in a SEARCH or SET statement'). COS (TX), where TX is an index-name, was refused with COBOL1637. cosc.cob: COS of a reference-modified numeric item WN (1:1) and COS of FUNCTION UPPER-CASE ("1") were each refused with COBOL1627 (class alphanumeric). COS (1.0E0) was refused with COBOL0900, because the floating-point literal requires COBOL-2002. cosok.cob was accepted and ran: COS of an SVPP9 item gave +0000.9999, COS (WB + FUNCTION INTEGER-PART (2.5)) gave 1, and a nested COS (FUNCTION COS (0) - 1) gave 1. cite: OK  §1989:A.2.10.3 AR1  (2.10.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR1.
